title: Finite projective generator gives an equivalence with modules
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $\mathcal C$ an essentially small $k$-linear abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with $k$-bilinear composition and finite-dimensional Hom spaces [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Let $P\in\mathcal C$ satisfy the following conditions: $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ takes every short exact sequence to a short exact sequence of $k$-vector spaces; if $f:Y\to Z$ has $f\circ h=0$ for all $h:P\to Y$ then $f=0$; and every $Y\in\mathcal C$ admits an epimorphism $P^{\oplus n}\to Y$ for some finite $n\geq0$. Put $R=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(P)$ with multiplication $rs=r\circ s$. A right $R$-module here is a $k$-vector space with a unital associative $k$-bilinear right action of $R$, with $k$-linear maps preserving the action as morphisms. The functor
$$H:\mathcal C\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}^{\mathrm{fd}}\!\text{-}R,\qquad H(Y)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,Y),\quad h\cdot r=h\circ r,\quad H(f)(h)=f\circ h$$
is an equivalence of $k$-linear categories. The zero endomorphism algebra, with $1=0$, is allowed.

source.place: Lemma 9.35, printed p.177, in its projective-generator formulation; finite presentation by finite sums is the argument in that proof.

proof.text: Composition and the $k$-linear structure give the stated right action: $(h\cdot r)\cdot s=h\circ r\circ s=h\cdot(rs)$ and $h\cdot1=h$. Postcomposition commutes with this action and with $k$-linear combinations, preserves identities and composition, and hence defines the $k$-linear functor $H$. Its values are finite-dimensional by hypothesis. It is faithful: if $H(f)=H(g)$, then $(f-g)\circ h=0$ for every $h:P\to Y$, so the assumed detection property gives $f-g=0$. Finite sums and the zero object below exist by [def-sp-abelian].

source.place: Lemma 9.35, printed p.177 (PDF p.189): finite presentations, matrix cokernels and fullness.

proof.text: Write $P^n=\bigoplus_{j=1}^nP$, with injections $\iota_j$ and projections $\pi_j$. The map $H(P^n)\to R^n$, $h\mapsto(\pi_jh)_j$, has inverse $(r_j)\mapsto\sum_j\iota_jr_j$, so is a right $R$-module isomorphism. For every $Y$, the map $\operatorname{Hom}(P^n,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(R^n,H(Y))$ induced by $H$ is bijective: a module map $a$ gives $b=\sum_j a(e_j)\pi_j$, and $H(b)((r_j))=\sum_j a(e_j)r_j=a((r_j))$. The equations $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_j\iota_j\pi_j=1$ prove both inverse identities. All maps are $k$-linear. This also covers $n=0$, when both Hom spaces are zero. Here $\operatorname{Hom}_R$ means the $k$-linear right-action-preserving maps of the statement.

source.place: Lemma 9.35, printed p.177 (PDF p.189): finite presentations, matrix cokernels and fullness.

proof.text: Let $F$ be $H$ with the right action forgotten, valued in all $k$-vector spaces. This target is abelian: kernels are ordinary linear kernels, cokernels are quotients by ranges, and injections and surjections have their respective kernel and cokernel universal properties. By hypothesis $F$ is additive and preserves short exact sequences. Thus [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], clause (a), says that $F$ preserves epimorphisms and cokernels. In particular, if $q$ is a cokernel of $u$ in $\mathcal C$, then $F(q)$ is surjective and $F(u),F(q)$ is a cokernel presentation. For an epimorphism $q$ alone, $F(q)$ is surjective as well. For vector spaces, these assertions mean precisely quotient by the image; surjectivity follows since a nonsurjective map has a nonzero quotient map annihilating its image.

source.place: Lemma 9.35, printed p.177 (PDF p.189): finite presentations, matrix cokernels and fullness.

proof.text: Every finite-dimensional right $R$-module $M$ has a finite free presentation. Indeed, choose a finite $k$-spanning family $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ of $M$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. The map $p:R^n\to M$, $(r_j)\mapsto\sum_jv_jr_j$, is surjective: $\sum_j\lambda_jv_j=\sum_jv_j(\lambda_j1_R)$ by bilinearity and unitality. A finite spanning family of $R=\operatorname{Hom}(P,P)$, placed in each coordinate, spans $R^n$ over $k$. Therefore $K=\ker p$ is finite-dimensional by [lem-trf-vector-space-quotient-dimension]. Choose a finite $k$-spanning family $w_1,\ldots,w_m$ in $K$; the map $a:R^m\to R^n$ with columns $w_i$ has image $K$, since $k$-scalar multiples are right multiplication by $\lambda1_R$. Hence $R^m\xrightarrow{a}R^n\xrightarrow{p}M\to0$ is the required presentation. This is a construction from finite spanning families, not an appeal to commutative Noetherian algebra.

source.place: Lemma 9.35, printed p.177 (PDF p.189): finite presentations, matrix cokernels and fullness.

proof.text: Given that presentation of $M$, Step 2 lifts $a$ to $u:P^m\to P^n$ with $H(u)=a$ in the displayed coordinates. Form its cokernel $q:P^n\to X$ using [def-sp-abelian]. By Step 3 and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a), the surjection $H(q):R^n\to H(X)$ has kernel $\operatorname{im}(a)=\ker p$ on underlying vector spaces. The rule $p(r)\mapsto H(q)(r)$ is therefore a well-defined bijection $M\to H(X)$. It is $k$-linear and right $R$-linear because both quotient maps are, so $H$ is essentially surjective. No lift of elements of an arbitrary categorical object was used.

source.place: Lemma 9.35, printed p.177 (PDF p.189): finite presentations, matrix cokernels and fullness.

proof.text: For each $X$, choose an epimorphism $q:P^n\to X$. Since every epimorphism is a cokernel [def-sp-abelian], choose $d:T\to P^n$ of which $q$ is a cokernel, and choose an epimorphism $t:P^m\to T$. Put $u=dt$. Then $q$ is also a cokernel of $u$: $bu=0$ implies $bdt=0$, hence $bd=0$ by cancellation of $t$, and $b$ factors uniquely through $q$. Now let $\alpha:H(X)\to H(Y)$ be a module morphism. Step 2 gives $b:P^n\to Y$ with $H(b)=\alpha H(q)$. Thus $H(bu)=\alpha H(qu)=0$, so $bu=0$ by Step 1. The cokernel property yields a unique $f:X\to Y$ with $fq=b$. Finally $H(f)H(q)=\alpha H(q)$, and $H(q)$ is surjective by Step 3 and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a), so $H(f)=\alpha$. Together with faithfulness this proves bijectivity on every Hom space.

source.place: Lemma 9.35, printed p.177 (PDF p.189): finite presentations, matrix cokernels and fullness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] to Steps 5 and 6, placing the categories in a common containing universe. Its conclusion supplies a quasi-inverse with natural unit and counit isomorphisms. This equivalence is $k$-linear: if its quasi-inverse on a morphism is defined by lifting its conjugate through $H$, then the inverse of the bijective $k$-linear Hom map of $H$ is $k$-linear, and conjugation by the chosen module isomorphisms is $k$-linear. Thus the quasi-inverse is $k$-linear too. If $P=0$, every object is zero because it is an epimorphic image of $P^n=0$; and if $R=0$, every unital right module has $v=v1=v0=0$. The preceding constructions include these cases and all zero ranks.
